# predicting burglaries
1. point data of burglaries
2. aggregate by 50ft matrix (fishnet)
3. burglaries per cell --> becomes a poisson distribution, bc bounded at zero + many many zero values

how to fix this distribution?
1. option 1: log y (becomes log y + 1 because many zero values) --> lying
2. option 2: POISSON DISTRIBUTION

reading poisson coefficient
- exp(beta) = multiplicative change in expected count per one unit change in x
- exp(0.20) = 1.22. each 1 unit increase in x leads to 22% more burglaries

assumptions
1. mean = variance (hence cannot have too many zeroes --> overdispersion --> in that case, need negative binomial)

# predicting crime
1. carto get to get 311 calls
2. make hotspots using LISA map
3. calculate distance to nearest hotspot
4. run OLS vs poisson 
5. pois <- glm(f1, family = "poisson", data = fishnet) --> GLM is Generalised Linear Model
6. compare map of predicted crime (from poisson model) to the actual data KDE map
